intervention_names: Combination Product: Stem Cell Educator therapy
arm_groups.label: Stem Cell Educator

brief_summary: Stem Cell Educator (SCE) therapy circulates a patient's blood through a blood cell separator, briefly cocultures the patient's immune cells with adherent Cord Blood Stem Cells (CB-SCs) in vitro, and returns only the "educated" autologous immune cells to the patient's circulation. Several mechanistic studies with clinical samples and animal models have demonstrated the proof of concept and clinical safety of SCE therapy. They suggest SCE therapy may function via CB-SC induction of immune tolerance in the autoimmune T cells and pathogenic monocytes/macrophages when these are exposed to the autoimmune regulator protein (AIRE) in the CB-SCs. In this project, the optimized SCE therapy for type 1 diabetes (T1D) and T2D will be tested in a prospective, single-arm, open-label, single-center study to assess its clinical efficacy and related molecular mechanisms in patients with diabetes.
brief_title: Stem Cell Educator Therapy in Diabetes

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients are screened for enrollment in the study if both clinical signs and laboratory tests meet the diagnosis standards of American Diabetes Association.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Exclusion criteria are any clinically significant diseases in liver, kidney, and heart. Additional exclusion criteria are no pregnancy, no immunosuppressive medication, no viral diseases or diseases associated with immunodeficiency.

official_title: Molecular Mechanisms Underlying Stem Cell Educator Therapy for the Treatment of Diabetes

primary_outcomes.measure: Changes of inflammation-related markers in diabetic patients after Stem Cell Educator therapy
